title: Edge Shadow Telemetry Contract for Private and Dedicated Evaluations (v1)
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:
This page specifies the telemetry contract and operating workflow for edge and private shadow evaluations running against Dedicated pools and customer-managed (Private) deployments. It trades off quality-check fidelity (coherence, hallucination, embedding drift) against privacy, cost and storage limits that apply in private environments. Audience: applied ML engineers, SREs who run shadow orchestration, and the oncall/regression teams handling triage and rollback.

Goals and scope:
- Define a minimal, documented telemetry payload every shadow evaluator emits in Private and Dedicated environments.
- Set sampling, anonymization, retention and encryption rules that satisfy customer privacy and KMS requirements.
- Define quality/regression gate metrics, thresholds and alerting for shadow rollouts and quant/optimize migrations.
- Provide a triage playbook for failing slices, with owners and rollback criteria.

Why this contract exists:
Private and Dedicated environments differ from Redwood-hosted evals: egress is limited, PII rules are stricter and hardware/quantization variants are heterogeneous. Ad hoc telemetry has been inconsistent and costly to analyze; a single contract gives us regression signal while respecting privacy and cost.

Telemetry payload spec (required fields):
Every shadow probe record carries these top-level fields (string or numeric only):
- probe_id: uuid for the probe run
- tenant_id: sha256-hex hashed tenant id or obfuscated alias; raw customer IDs MUST NOT leave the private boundary without agreement
- deployed_model: model name + version (e.g., redwood-7b-v2-quant8)
- deployment_variant: one of [hosted, dedicated, private]
- quant_profile: quant profile label (e.g., q8_fast_fp16_fallback)
- hardware_tag: e.g., a100-40gb, t4-16gb, edge-x86-32g
- prompt_family: probe set token (e.g., billing_faq_anchors_v3)
- seed_context_hash: sha1 of canonicalized prompt/context (dedupe only; non-reversible)
- latency_ms: end-to-end latency in ms (int)
- tokens_input: input token count (int)
- tokens_generated: generated token count (int)
- top_level_metrics: comma-separated metrics, e.g., coherence:0.82,hallucination:0.03,embed_cos_sim:0.67
- error_code: empty or a standard code (Appendix C)
- timestamp_utc: ISO8601 timestamp

Optional fields (only where privacy and egress permit):
- raw_response_snippet: up to 512 characters, post-redaction
- annotator_score: human score 0..1 when an annotator is used
- kv_cache_hit: true/false

Sampling and rate limits:
- Default private shadow sampling: 1% of production traffic or 500 probes/day per tenant (whichever is smaller), unless a campaign configures otherwise.
- Dedicated pools without egress may raise sampling for controlled experiments with customer approval; record it in the deployment manifest.
- Stratified sampling by prompt_family must be supported so rare slices are represented (min 5 probes per slice per day when available).

Privacy, encryption, and retention:
- Telemetry leaving the customer network is encrypted with the customer KMS key (AES-256-GCM envelope encryption).
- tenant_id is always hashed; reversible identifiers need documented consent and a signed customer exception.
- raw_response_snippet passes through the automated PII redaction pipeline before export, using redaction library version >= v1.4.
- Default retention: 14 days for detailed probe payloads, 365 days for aggregated daily rollups. Longer retention requires a retention SLA and on-prem analytics hooks.

Metric definitions and SLOs (shadow-eval quality gates):
- Coherence (slice median): 0..1; alert when < 0.70; action: open incident and notify model-owner. Multi-turn cohesion per the coherence rubric.
- Hallucination rate (slice): fraction; alert when > 0.08; action: open P1 triage if sustained for 6 hours. Benign OOD prompts excluded after review.
- Embedding cosine shift: delta; alert when > 0.12; action: schedule regression-bisect and tag model-version. Compared with anchor baseline.
- Latency p95: ms; alert when > 2x baseline or > 1200ms; action: throttle rollout, roll back if the tail persists. Baseline per hardware_tag.

Alerting and integration:
- Publish shadow-eval metrics to the Ops dashboard in a tenant-scoped anonymized view, using shadow.coherence.*, shadow.hallucination.*, shadow.latency.*.
- Auto-create incidents when a threshold is breached for >= 30 minutes across >=3 prompt_families.
- Annotate incidents with whether failing probes used quantized variants.

Workflow: Shadow rollouts and gating:
1. Prepare: define the campaign (prompt_families, sampling rate, quant_profile, traffic window). Owner: Applied ML engineer.
2. Dry run: offline shadow run on a representative dataset; record baseline and open an acceptance ticket.
3. Shadow deploy: route sampled traffic to the shadow instance (invisible to users) and emit telemetry per contract.
4. Monitor: live slice metrics on the dashboard; automated gates evaluate every 5 minutes.
5. Escalate: on threshold breach, run the triage playbook.
6. Decide: promote via canary, keep shadowing, or roll back.

Regression triage playbook (short-form):
- Initial assessment (15 minutes):
  1. Confirm the alert: metric, prompt_families, hardware_tag.
  2. Check context: quant_profile, kv_cache_hit, batch size, runtime kernel revision.
  3. Correlate with infra alerts (GPU errors, memory pressure).
- Isolation (30 minutes):
  4. Reproduce with deterministic local replay (replay-tool with probe_id).
  5. Run regression bisect where applicable.
- Remediation:
  6. Quant-induced regressions: switch to the fallback profile (q_fallback) and validate.
  7. Model-quality regressions: escalate to model-owner; roll back if degradation persists > 2 hours.
  8. Record root cause; add a probe to the longtail suite for novel failure modes.

Ownership and responsibilities:
- Applied ML: probe families, baseline acceptance criteria, annotation rubrics.
- Eng-SRE: telemetry pipelines, encryption, retention, dashboards; runs the incident runbook when infra is involved.
- Runtime/Serving: exposes runtime tags (kernel revision, batch size) and kernel rollback knobs.
- Data-privacy/legal: approves tenant identifier exceptions and retention extensions.

Appendix A - Example telemetry payload (redacted):
- probe_id = 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
- tenant_id = 9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08
- deployed_model = redwood-7b-v2-quant8
- deployment_variant = private

Appendix B - On-prem agent config (excerpt):
agent name: shadow-forwarder
batch_size: 500
encrypt_with_kms: true
kms_key_alias: alias/customer-tenant-123
max_outbound_ops_per_min: 60
retention_days: 14
allowed_fields: probe_id, deployed_model, quant_profile, hardware_tag, prompt_family, seed_context_hash, latency_ms, tokens_input, tokens_generated, top_level_metrics, error_code, timestamp_utc

Common commands:
- Local shadow replay: replay-tool --from probe_log --filter prompt_family=billing_faq_anchors_v3 --replay-count 200
- Recent failing probes: rw-metrics query --metric shadow.hallucination.rate --since 2h --filter quant_profile=q8_fast_fp16_fallback --output csv
- Temporary egress approval for extended sampling: infra-ticket create --type egress-exception --reason "Quant stress test" --owner eng-applied-ml

Governance and exceptions:
- Deviations from the minimal payload need a documented exception signed by Data-Privacy and, for tenant-owned data, the customer.
- Retention beyond 90 days needs Security signoff and a forensic justification.

Onboarding checklist:
1. Add the contract to the deployment manifest (deployment-config).
2. Check the agent config against allowed_fields and encryption settings.
3. Dry run with an anonymized sample; confirm metrics match the local baseline within tolerance.
4. Schedule a 2-week shadow window and monitor.
5. If stable, add probes to the daily longtail sweep and push new failures to probe-farm.

Appendix C - Error-code table:
- E000: OK
- E100: Model timeout
- E200: Runtime OOM
- E300: Quantization fallback triggered
- E400: PII-redaction-failed
